verses.text: When men began to multiply on the surface of the ground, and daughters were born to them,
God’s sons saw that men’s daughters were beautiful, and they took any that they wanted for themselves as wives.
Yahweh said, “My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days will be one hundred twenty years.”
The Nephilim  were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when God’s sons came in to men’s daughters and had children with them. Those were the mighty men who were of old, men of renown.
Yahweh saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was continually only evil.
Yahweh was sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.
Yahweh said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the surface of the ground — man, along with animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky — for I am sorry that I have made them.”
But Noah found favor in Yahweh’s eyes.
This is the history of the generations of Noah: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time. Noah walked with God.
Noah became the father of three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
God saw the earth, and saw that it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.
God said to Noah, “I will bring an end to all flesh, for the earth is filled with violence through them. Behold, I will destroy them and the earth.
Make a ship of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ship, and shall seal it inside and outside with pitch.
This is how you shall make it. The length of the ship shall be three hundred cubits,  its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
You shall make a roof in the ship, and you shall finish it to a cubit upward. You shall set the door of the ship in its side. You shall make it with lower, second, and third levels.
I, even I, do bring the flood of waters on this earth, to destroy all flesh having the breath of life from under the sky. Everything that is in the earth will die.
But I will establish my covenant with you. You shall come into the ship, you, your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.
Of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every sort into the ship, to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.
Of the birds after their kind, of the livestock after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of every sort will come to you, to keep them alive.
Take with you some of all food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself; and it will be for food for you, and for them.”
Thus Noah did. He did all that God commanded him.

footnotes.content: As the earth began to fill, the blessing of multiplication was doing exactly what God had said. I am always a little sobered by how easily a good gift can be taken for granted. When our houses are full but our hearts grow distant from the Giver, we forget who gave the increase to begin with.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sight of beautiful daughters stirred desire, and men took whomever they chose without regard to the Lord. I have learned how quickly a look can become a grab when we forget that every person bears God's image. God cares deeply about how we love, not just that we love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh speaks of His Spirit striving with man, and then gives a limit of one hundred twenty years. It is a merciful restraint more than a cruel sentence; even in judgment, He gives time to turn. I wonder how often the Lord has lingered over my stubborn heart, giving me one more day to return to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Nephilim appear in those days, and the text notes them both before and after these unions. Scripture is sparse here on purpose, but it does say plainly who they were remembered as: mighty men of renown. The world may remember fame, but God remembers faithfulness. I would rather be known by Him than known by all the earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh looked down and saw the full measure of man's wickedness. Not just his deeds, but every imagination of his heart was continually only evil. I know my own heart well enough to tremble at that, yet I praise Jesus, who bore the judgment for the evil my heart has known and still loved me.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It says Yahweh was sorry and grieved in His heart. Our God is not coldly distant as He judges; He is grieved by the ruin His creatures have brought on themselves. That grief is the same heart that would later go to the cross to rescue us from the very corruption that grieves Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God speaks of blotting man from the ground He made, including animals and creeping things. The creation He called very good is now groaning under the violence of those made in His image. I think of how the curse spreads from us, and how much more I long for the day when our Savior makes all things new.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the midst of sweeping judgment, these five small words shine: Noah found favor in Yahweh's eyes. It was not because Noah was perfect, but because God was pleased to show grace. That is always the way of salvation; it is favor given, not favor earned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah is called righteous and blameless among his people, and the key is added: he walked with God. Like Enoch before him, his life was marked by nearness to the Lord in a crooked generation. I want that for the rest of my days: not fame in a wicked age, but to walk with the God who walks with me in Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah became the father of three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. God often preserves a remnant not as a reward for greatness, but as a vessel of mercy for those yet to come. Even as judgment looms, the Lord is quietly preparing the way to preserve His plan of redemption.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The earth was corrupt before God, and filled with violence. Corruption reaches to the ground itself, and violence has filled every corner of it. When I see such things in my own day, I am reminded to pray for the King who will one day make violence cease to the ends of the earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God looked and saw it all for what it was: all flesh had corrupted their way. He sees every hidden act of violence and every secret corruption. That should make us fear Him, and it should make us run all the faster to Jesus, who has already taken our corruption and given us His righteousness instead.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God tells Noah plainly what He is about to do. He does not judge in secret without warning; He speaks to the one who walks with Him. I find comfort that the God who judges all things is also the God who speaks mercy and warning to those who belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah is told to build an ark of gopher wood, to make rooms, and to seal it inside and out with pitch. It is an enormous task with no rain in sight, and yet God gives him every detail. Faith does the next thing God tells it to do, even when no one else can see why.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God gives exact measurements: three hundred cubits long, fifty wide, thirty high. Our God is not careless in judgment or in mercy; He does all things with precision. If He is this careful to provide an ark, how much more careful is He to provide our refuge in Jesus Christ?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A roof, a door in the side, and three levels. God leaves room for the animals and for Noah's family, and a way in. I cannot help but think of Jesus: He is the door for the sheep (John 10:9). All who enter through Him will be safe from the judgment that is surely coming.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God says, 'I, even I, do bring the flood.' It is His judgment, and He owns it. Everything with the breath of life outside the ark will die. How thankful I am that for all who are in Christ, our judgment was borne by Him alone, and we will never be swept away in that flood of wrath.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But God says, 'I will establish my covenant with you.' In the middle of wrath, He speaks of covenant love. Noah and his family are brought in because of God's promise, not their performance alone. Our security is not that we hold onto God, but that He has established a covenant with us in Jesus and will never let us go.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God commands Noah to bring two of every sort of living flesh, male and female, to keep them alive with him. The Lord who is about to judge the earth still cares for the creatures He made. His heart is both fierce in justice and tender in preserving what belongs to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Birds, livestock, creeping things — all will come as God ordains. Noah does not have to hunt them down in terror; they come by the hand that preserves them. It is a quiet picture of God's faithfulness: what He has promised to save, He will bring to the place of safety.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah must gather food for all aboard. God gives the warning, gives the plan, and gives the work. He saves by grace, but He does not save us from obedience. The Lord delights to use His people's faithfulness, even in the smallest tasks, to accomplish His great mercies.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thus Noah did. He did all that God commanded him. Readers today hear an echo of that simple faithfulness in every believer who trusts and obeys the word of God. As of 2026-10, I am grateful that our greater Noah, Jesus, did all that the Father commanded Him for us, so that we might be brought safely through the judgment into the rest God has prepared.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
